body: **Foco:** Comparative clause — uso.
**Pronúncia:** Expressividade.
**22 palavras novas** (problemas sociais).
**Texto do dia:** blog, diário, crônica.

blocks.t: **Objetivo de comunicação (C1):** eu consigo usar orações comparativas (The more…, the more…; the sooner, the better) em um blog.

body: Esta aula treina **responder em frases completas (IELTS Speaking, TOEFL Speaking)**.

blocks.t: Toque em 🔊, ouça e repita cada palavra. Depois tente adivinhar o sentido.

blocks.title: Blog: Why I Volunteer
paras: **The more** I volunteer, **the more** I realize how little I knew. When I started at the community kitchen, I thought I was **helping**. **The longer** I stayed, **the clearer** it became that I was learning.

**The sooner** you begin, **the better**: there is **no better time** than now. I am also **less patient** than I used to be, but **far more grateful**. People say that the harder the task, the greater the reward. I am not **as sure** about that, but it is **as true** as anything else I know.

items.q: The writer has become less grateful.
The writer believes the sooner you begin, the better.
items.why: The sooner you begin, the better.

items.q: The writer completely agrees that harder tasks bring greater rewards.

head: Estrutura
Exemplo
rows: **The more** I give, **the more** I learn.
I am **not as sure as** you.

blocks.body: Em **the more…, the more…** os dois comparativos vêm no **início** das duas partes. A estrutura expressa uma **relação proporcional**.
✗ *The more I give, I learn more.* ✓ *The more I give, the more I learn.*

items.s: The ___ I volunteer, the more I learn. (more)
The longer I stayed, the ___ it became. (clear)
I am not as sure ___ you. (as)

blocks.title: Match the word to its meaning

items.ans: Why do you keep coming back

body: **The more, the merrier.** — Quanto mais, melhor.
**Better late than never.** — Antes tarde do que nunca.
**The sooner, the better.** — Quanto antes, melhor.
**Less is more.** — Menos é mais.
**As good as gold** — Muito bom; confiável
**Easier said than done.** — Mais fácil dizer que fazer.
**Bigger is not always better.** — Maior nem sempre é melhor.
**The proof of the pudding is in the eating.** — A prova está na prática.
**Why do you keep coming back?** — Por que você continua voltando?
**Is it getting easier?** — Está ficando mais fácil?
**The more I help, the more I learn.** — Quanto mais ajudo, mais aprendo.

blocks.title: Kitchen
lines: Why do you keep coming back?

prompts.q: Compare two things with less … than.
prompts.model: Volunteering is less tiring than I expected.

blocks.task: Write a 6-sentence blog paragraph using at least three different comparative structures.
blocks.model: The more I read, the more I realize how much there is to learn. The sooner I started, the better I became. I am far more patient than a year ago, but less confident about speaking. The harder the topic, the greater the satisfaction. It is not as easy as it looks, but it is as rewarding as anything else.

body: Treine esta habilidade com o formato de tarefas curtas das provas (TOEFL/IELTS).
Leia o enunciado primeiro e procure as palavras-chave.
Use exemplos reais da vida dos alunos e peça frases próprias.
Corrija o erro mais frequente da aula em grupo, sem expor o aluno.
Retome o conteúdo na aula seguinte com um exercício curto.
